liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Iko Iko was played slowly with a funky groove for ten minutes as a Jerry celebration [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd82-08-01 t01 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-08-01 t02 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-08-01 t03 CC Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-08-01 t04 Tennessee Jed**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-08-01 t05 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-08-01 t06 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-08-01 t07 China Cat Sunflower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd82-08-01 t08 I Know You Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-08-01.141594.sbd.healy.streeter.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 142 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1982-08-01.158150.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 141 min [4]
- **gd1982-08-01.nak700.seligman.ford.82883.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 131 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [11]
- **gd1982-08-01.124193.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 141 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Heat reached 105 degrees, causing Jerry to look distressed during the short first set [13]
- Bob referenced zoo animals, with elephants audible, during the first performance of Iko Iko [14]
- Show delayed due to heat; Jerry's stage area lacked shade for the first hour [15]
- Audience could walk to the front stage; beer cost seven dollars in hot milk jugs [16]
- Band was exhausted from a midnight birthday party and long drives before the show [21]
- Venue held six thousand people, featuring tall trees and red mud on the perimeter [22]
- Second set flowed continuously without stopping, connecting songs seamlessly, unlike the first set [17]
- Soundboard recording is much better than the audience tape, which contained a crying child [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-08-01.141594.sbd.healy.streeter.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Frank Streeter and Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips (Sony… [1]
- **gd1982-08-01.158150.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5 (Maxell MX-90) [4]
- **gd1982-08-01.nak700.seligman.ford.82883.sbeok.flac16**: taped by David Seligman; transferred by Alex Ford; source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM-700s > Sony TC-D5M > MC > Cassette x2 [11]. Also: Recording contains several cassette generations with Dolby processing, making the SBD preferable; Second-generation cassettes provided by Jake Feinberg, transfer and edits by Alex Ford [11][23]
- **gd1982-08-01.124193.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by dusborne; source: 2 Source Matrix by dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:10226) SBD>MC>DAT>CD EAC/SHN by Willy and Audience (shnid:82883) Source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM-700s > Sony TC-D5M >… [2]
